root_cause.text: The function `hfs_correct_next_unused_CNID()` accesses the `node` pointer (specifically `node->prev`) after calling `hfs_bnode_put(node)`, which releases the reference and can free the node, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch flips the order of `node_id = node->prev;` and `hfs_bnode_put(node);` so that the pointer is read before the reference is dropped. The commit message states: "This code calls hfs_bnode_put(node) which drops the refcount and then dreferences "node" on the next line. It's only safe to use "node" when we're holding a reference so flip these two lines around."
